label: input token v/c/u/a early in the original phase or at the first two copy steps
explanation: A token-identity reset-gate unit. Almost all activation (98% of mass) happens when the current input is v, c, u or a, ranked by rate in that order: v 12%, c 11%, u 5%, a 3%. v and c together carry about 78% of the mass. It never fires at t=0 or on the <DEL> step, and it is nearly silent in the copy phase after recall_idx 2. Its rate is highest at original positions 1-2 and at copy steps recall_idx 1-2, where the input is orig(0) or orig(1). Even inside that context it fires on only about 15% of v/c/u steps. Which ones fire depends on context I could not capture: preceding a/c/w/k/2/t/o/<DEL> roughly doubles precision (F1 0.39, mass recall 0.76 on dev). The largest activations are c right after a, and v at the second copy step. The recorded predicate captures about 90% of dev mass but has low precision (0.15). It does not fire on any other letter or digit.
